title: Cross-Functional Sprint Onboard Kit (7/30/90)
summary: Practical, lightweight playbook for ramping new hires into cross-functional sprint teams. Designed for engineering, product, and design ICs who will ship features within the first 90 days. Combines tactical checklists, sample interview rubric snippets, and measurable 7/30/90 checkpoints so managers and new hires have a shared rhythm.
audience: Hiring managers, people ops partners, technical interviewers, hiring panel coordinators
objectives: Reduce time-to-impact for cross-functional ICs by giving a repeatable 7/30/90 cadence
Provide hiring panels with a concise rubric tuned for execution-oriented product work
Create a manager-friendly checklist that scales across remote and hybrid teams
quick-start-1st-week: Day 0: account access + hardware checklist + buddy assigned. Day 1: orientation (HR, benefits, security), team intro, 1:1 with manager to set expectations. Days 2-3: codebase walkthrough or product area tour, set up dev/test environment, small 'first-commit' task. Day 4: shadow sprint planning and triage. Day 5: 30-minute calibration with buddy + document blockers.
7-day-checkpoints: Access: all logins, email, Slack, CI, internal dashboards. Visibility: sprint board assigned, active on at least one repo/board. Social: 3 intro 1:1s scheduled (PM, tech lead, design). Quick win: merged first small change or build verification.
30-day-objectives: Deliver a scoped piece of work that completes a sprint ticket end-to-end (design → implementation → QA). Measure: merged PR + deploy-to-staging + post-merge checklist completed. Collateral: README updates and short architecture note.
60-day-objectives: Own a feature slice across the team for a sprint (planning through delivery). Measure: lead at least one planning session, unblock two cross-team dependencies, and drive a rollback/incident runbook if needed.
90-day-signals-of-success: Consistent delivery with low guidance (manager confidence in independent execution), positive feedback from peers in at least 3 domains (code/design/process), and contribution to a cross-functional retrospective with concrete improvement proposals.
manager-responsibilities: Prepare first-week schedule, assign a buddy, set clear alpha/beta expectations for 30/60/90, run weekly 1:1s with explicit agenda (blockers, ramp topics), own feedback and calibration with people ops at day 30/90.
onboarding-checklist: Pre-day 1: hardware shipped and imaged; accounts provisioned
Day 1: HR orientation completed; security/e2e training assigned
Within 48 hours: first-buddy intro, initial 1:1 with manager scheduled
Within 7 days: dev env validated with smoke PR
Within 30 days: first scoped delivery merged and triaged
Within 60 days: feature ownership during sprint; start measuring throughput
Within 90 days: performance calibration with manager and people ops
interview-rubric-high-level: Execution (40%): deliverables orientation — candidates must show history of shipping features and closing loops. Look for concrete examples, ownership level, and ability to break down tasks.
Collaboration (25%): communication with PM/design/infra, conflict resolution, asynchronous docs. Expect stories showing cross-team influence without formal authority.
Core skills (25%): technical competency relevant to role (system design for backend, component design for frontend, prototyping for design). Evaluate trade-offs and constraints handling.
Learning mindset (10%): speed of learning, curiosity, how they handle a missed ship or postmortem. Prefer candidates who produce short learnings and system improvements.
Scoring guidance: 1=insufficient, 3=meets, 5=exceeds. Hiring pulse: average >=3.5 with no dimension below 2 for offer consideration.
sample-interview-questions: Tell me about the last feature you owned from planning to launch. What trade-offs did you make?
Describe a time you disagreed with a PM/design decision. How did you resolve it?
For a component/system you built, how did you measure success post-launch? What metrics did you track and why?
Give an example of a cross-team dependency that blocked you. How did you unblock it?
When you have limited time, how do you decide what to cut from a scope?
offer-qualification-criteria: Minimum: comp track record consistent with level, technical screen average >=3, at least one engineering ref, clear signals on collaboration. For senior levels require 2 strong system-design narratives and evidence of mentoring/leadership.
suggested-roles-for-buddy: Prefer same subdomain: e.g., backend buddy for backend hire. Buddy should be mid-senior level, not the hiring manager, and have bandwidth for 3x30-min check-ins in first two weeks.
escalation-paths: If onboarding blockers persist beyond 7 days (access, infra, or unclear scope), manager escalates to People Ops partner and infra oncall. For hiring pipeline issues (offer delay, candidate ghosting) escalate to recruiting lead.
